summary: Keepalive TTL compression during canary surge causes model-pin entropy and silent fallback to compat variant
description: Customer reports intermittent routing to compatibility (fallback) variant during a scheduled canary. Traffic appeared pinned to legacy variant for sessions that should have remained pinned to the new canary variant. Investigation shows correlation with a recent ingress optimization: keepalive TTL compression (cookie/lease TTL normalization) rolled to edge-proxy in the same window.
impact: Several Brightline Health tenant sessions experienced divergent model outputs and increased latency due to silent fallback to compat variant. Estimated affected requests: ~1.8k over a 12-minute window. Customer reports degraded user experience for their triage assistant flows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy canary weight 20% for redwood/gptx-3.0-quantized-v1 in prod-us-east
2) Enable ingress keepalive TTL compression flag (edge-proxy v1.18.2) which shortens session cookie TTLs under high connection churn
3) Generate synthetic session traffic matching customer's prefix/hash (tenant header X-Tenant: brightline) and simulate a 40% keepalive reconnect rate
4) Observe model routing fingerprints and pin assignments in the route-coordinator telemetry (see logs)
observed_behavior_logs: 2026-03-13T09:12:24Z ingress-proxy[edge-01] INFO keepalive-ttl-compress applied cookie_ttl=120->18 tenant=brightline session_id=sh:3b2f
2026-03-13T09:12:27Z route-coordinator WARN pin_evict tenant=brightline session_id=sh:3b2f prev_pin=canary_variant commit_ttl=120 computed_ttl=18
2026-03-13T09:12:30Z orchestrator INFO fallback_route tenant=brightline session_id=sh:3b2f target=compat_variant reason=pin_absent
metrics: pin_evictions=172 over=12m; fallback_rate=9.1% for brightline routes; p95_latency +42ms on compat_variant
investigation_notes: Initial triage: no model-serving 5xx spikes and Dedicated capacity healthy. Error budget not exceeded.

Edge logs show TTL normalization shortened session leases for high-churn keepalive connections. Short TTLs triggered early pin eviction in route-coordinator because pin tenure calculations relied on cookie TTL distribution.

Race condition: when keepalive reconnect occurred within compressed TTL windows, the route-coordinator reconciler treated the session as a new cohort (no pin) momentarily and applied fallback logic to the compat variant before the canary assignment could reattach.
Reproducible in staging by toggling keepalive compression and generating churned reconnects. Repro captured in route-coordinator integration test harness PR referenced above.
Not a tokenization or model quality issue—pure routing/pinning state coherence issue introduced by TTL transform.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Received initial report from Brightline at 09:20 UTC. Customer saw mixed responses in user session IDs they provided.
Elena Novak (Brightline Health): Confirming we saw degraded outputs around 09:11-09:23. Triage users reported 20-40% of flows returning legacy responses.

Jordan Lee (SRE): Observed keepalive TTL compress rollout to edge pool ~09:10. Pin eviction counts spike correlated with ingress change. Captured traces and session IDs sent to route-coordinator team.
Miguel Santos (Assignee): Rolling ingress-config flag back in prod-us-east, monitoring for reappearance. Also opening hotfix to pin-tenure calculation to ignore compressed TTLs below threshold.
Jordan Lee (SRE): Rollback completed at 09:38. Confirming eviction rate returned to baseline. Patch branch created for deterministic pin TTL derivation. See PR linked.
resolution: Mitigated: rolled back keepalive TTL compression flag on edge-proxy in prod-us-east at 2026-03-13T09:38Z which stopped further pin evictions. Deployed a hotfix to route-coordinator to treat cookie_ttl < 30s as 'transient' and preserve pin tenure; landed and rolled to canary (orchestrator PR merged).
root_cause: Ingress optimization (keepalive TTL compression) reduced apparent session TTLs under connection churn. Route-coordinator interpreted compressed TTLs as authoritative pin tenure and evicted pins prematurely, causing short-lived loss of model version affinity and a fallback to compatibility variant.
resolution_notes: 1) Immediate: rollback TTL compression in edge-proxy for prod-us-east (09:38 UTC).
2) Short term: route-coordinator hotfix to ignore cookie TTLs below configurable threshold (patched & canaried 03-13).
3) Medium term: add a TTL-synthesis layer that coalesces keepalive metadata with session fingerprint to avoid TTL-driven pin churn.
4) Customer: Brightline notified of rollback and steps; monitoring showed no further incidents for their tenant.
5) Post-incident: retro scheduled and runbook updated.
